findings.title: Working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable uses wrong time units and wrong day, making the new working-hours gate ineffective
findings.body: The newly added working-hours gate compares `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` (minutes since midnight, e.g. 570 for 09:30) against `workingHour.startTime`/`workingHour.endTime`. However, `WorkingHours` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) defines `startTime`/`endTime` as minutes since midnight in the *organizer's* timezone, while `slotStartTime` is a UTC Dayjs object — so the comparison mixes UTC minutes-of-day with organizer-local minutes-of-day and will reject or accept slots incorrectly across timezones. Additionally, `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` uses the UTC day-of-week of the slot, but `WorkingHours.days` are defined in the organizer's local timezone, so near midnight the wrong weekday can be selected. The consequence is that after this change, slots can be wrongly filtered out (or wrongly kept) for any organizer whose timezone differs from UTC, breaking availability for round-robin/fixed-host events — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix. Note the same gate is also applied to non-override days, so this affects normal availability, not just date overrides.

findings.title: Date-override matching in checkIfIsAvailable compares organizer-local dates against UTC slot dates, so overrides are matched to the wrong day
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the override day is computed as `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` where `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, and this is compared to `slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD')` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()`. The left side is the override's calendar date expressed in the organizer's timezone (a local date), while the right side is the slot's UTC calendar date. These are different calendars, so for organizers not in UTC the override will be matched against the wrong day (off by the timezone offset), causing slots on the override day to be incorrectly rejected (treated as 'not within the date override') and slots on adjacent days to be incorrectly accepted. The subsequent range checks also mix the organizer-local shifted instants (`date.start + utcOffset`) with UTC slot times, compounding the error. This directly undermines the PR's goal of honoring fixed-host date overrides for round-robin events.

findings.title: Equality check between Dayjs objects in date-override logic never matches, making all-day overrides behave as ranged overrides
findings.body: Line 114 uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` to detect an all-day (unavailable) override where start equals end. This is a reference equality comparison between two distinct Dayjs instances, which is always false. As a result, an all-day date override (start === end, meaning 'unavailable all day') is not detected as such; the code falls through to the range checks, and since `slotEndTime.isBefore(start) || slotEndTime.isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` can both be false for slots inside that day, `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns undefined while `dateOverrideExist` is true — so the function returns `true` (available) for slots on a day the organizer explicitly marked unavailable. This is a data-integrity/booking-correctness bug: round-robin events can be booked on days the fixed host marked as fully unavailable.

findings.title: Selected-slot filtering returns false when a user has no reserved slot and the event is not a seated event, inverting the intended logic
findings.body: In the `selectedSlots` handling block, the per-user filter does: `if (!busy?.length && eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot === null) { return false; }`. For a non-seated event (`seatsPerTimeSlot === null`) where the user has no reserved (selected) slot, `busy` is empty, so the user is filtered out of `slot.userIds`, and the slot is subsequently dropped by `.filter((slot) => !!slot.userIds?.length)`. That means any slot without a corresponding `selectedSlots` row removes all users and eliminates the slot entirely — the opposite of the intent (a user with no reservation should be considered available). This will incorrectly hide available slots whenever `selectedSlots` exist for the event but not for every user/slot combination.

findings.title: Date-override activation check uses UTC day boundaries against invitee-local day, misclassifying overrides near midnight
findings.body: `activeOverrides` is computed with `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf('day'), null, '[)')`. `startOfInviteeDay` is a Dayjs in the invitee's timezone (its underlying instant is the invitee's local midnight), but `dayjs.utc(override.start)` is the override start as a UTC instant. Comparing a UTC instant against an invitee-local day range means an override that starts on the invitee's local day can be excluded (or one from the adjacent UTC day included) whenever the invitee timezone is not UTC — e.g. an override for 00:30–02:00 local in a UTC+6 invitee timezone starts at 18:30 UTC the previous day and fails the `isBetween` check. The override is then silently ignored and the regular working hours are used, so the timezone fix does not apply consistently.

findings.title: Override offset is computed from the override start instant only, ignoring DST differences between start and end
findings.body: The override-to-invitee conversion computes a single `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` using `dayjs(override.start...)` and applies that same offset to both `override.start` and `override.end`. If a DST transition occurs between the override start and end (or the offset differs at the end instant), the end time is shifted by the wrong amount, producing an incorrect override window length. The correct approach is to compute the offset separately for the start and end instants (or convert each instant to the invitee timezone independently). Consequence: date overrides spanning a DST change yield wrong slot boundaries in the invitee's timezone.

findings.title: Seat-occupancy merge uses `typeof x !== undefined` instead of a value check, so the branch is effectively dead
findings.body: `if (typeof availabilityCheckProps.currentSeats !== undefined)` is always true (`typeof` always returns a string, which is never `undefined`), so the intended guard — only merge occupied seats into an existing `currentSeats` array — does not work. When `currentSeats` is `undefined`, the `.map` call on line 532 throws a TypeError at runtime whenever `occupiedSeats.length` is non-zero and `currentSeats` was not previously set. This is a latent crash in the seats path introduced by restructuring this block.

findings.title: New timezone test only asserts identical UTC output and does not actually verify timezone-dependent override behavior
findings.body: The added test `scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone` requests the schedule with `timeZone: Timezones['+6:00']` (Asia/Dhaka) but asserts the exact same UTC slot list (`08:30:00.000Z` … `11:30:00.000Z`) and the same `dateString` bucket as the IST request, with the comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time'. Because `getSchedule` returns slots keyed by the invitee-timezone date and the requested window (`plus1DateStringT18:30Z` to `plus2DateStringT18:29:59Z`) only covers one UTC day, the test cannot distinguish correct from incorrect timezone handling — a regression that ignored the invitee timezone entirely would still pass. The test does not verify that the override date is interpreted in the organizer's timezone and rendered on the correct invitee-local day, which is the behavior the PR claims to fix. A meaningful test would use a window/override where the invitee-local day differs from the UTC day (e.g. an override late in the UTC day that falls on the next local day in Dhaka) and assert the shifted slot set.

findings.title: No test covers date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, which is the primary fix in this PR
findings.body: The PR description states the main fix is that 'date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events', but the only new/changed test (`Check for Date overrides`) uses a single-user event with `hosts: []` and no `schedulingType: 'ROUND_ROBIN'`. There is no test that creates a round-robin event with a fixed host plus a round-robin host, adds a date override for the fixed host, and asserts that slots outside the override are removed. The `checkIfIsAvailable` changes that implement this behavior (dateOverrides/workingHours/organizerTimeZone parameters and the fixed-host `every` loop) are therefore untested for the round-robin path, leaving the core fix without regression coverage.
